subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: Should OpenClaw accept this official external MXC sandbox plugin's native dependency graph and upstream argv-carried base64 config boundary after the stray sandbox export is removed?
rationale: Automation can remove the accidental export, but accepting packaged native executables, a `node-pty` install script, and config-on-argv behavior is a repository security-boundary decision.

options.title: Approve After Export Cleanup
options.body: Remove the stray sandbox barrel export first, then let an admin/secops owner approve the exact-head dependency graph and documented MXC argv boundary.

options.title: Pause For Upstream Transport
options.body: Hold this PR until MXC provides a non-argv config transport or OpenClaw can wrap one without weakening the sandbox boundary.

options.title: Decline First-Party Native MXC
options.body: Close or split the work if maintainers do not want OpenClaw to own this native sandbox dependency surface as an official plugin.

recommendation.title: Approve After Export Cleanup
recommendation.body: Remove the stray sandbox barrel export first, then let an admin/secops owner approve the exact-head dependency graph and documented MXC argv boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: He is assigned on the PR and has the clearest current sandbox/plugin SDK ownership trail for deciding whether the remaining boundary is acceptable.
